svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: macOS · Gallery · item view · a preview · Import the originals from iPhone 18 Pro? · 1310×800
svg.desc: Mirrors the preview page's just-in-time question in the Mac's Gallery item view WHEN A DEVICE NEARBY HOLDS THE ORIGINALS (nearby originals, docs/nearby-originals-plan.md §7; new 2026-09-28, drawn from the code): gallery.item.preview.nearby.svg with the Light button clicked. A click on any greyed control — one of the six buttons, a locked page of the tab bar — runs EditorPreviewPage.ask(_:), which reads availability(of: .pixelEdit) and raises the page's .alert in the words of FetchPromptContent (App/FetchPrompt.swift — shared with every other door's .fetchPrompt, whose word() also asks the devices nearby what they hold: `nearby.want`). The offer is fetchOffer's `.nearby(NearbyOffer, alsoOnPicPlace:)` — NearbyService.offer, ahead of PicPlace (N12), only while that device answers (LetsLapse open on it, the same network: N7, N15). For Light (Tapped.group(.light), subject 'Light') on this preview, whose originals are only on iPhone 18 Pro (alsoOnPicPlace false): title 'Import \(noun.text) from \(nearby.deviceName)?' → 'Import the originals from iPhone 18 Pro?' (two lines at 216: 'Import the originals from iPhone' 208.5, '18 Pro?'); message '\(subject) needs \(noun.text) — \(shortfall.sizeText) on \(nearby.deviceName), nearby. You can keep browsing while \(noun.pronoun) come\(noun.isPlural ? "" : "s") over.' → 'Light needs the originals — 214 files · 1,16 GB on iPhone 18 Pro, nearby. You can keep browsing while they come over.' (four lines); 'Import and Continue' → download(shortfall, landing:) → picplace.fetch, which takes the device nearby first (importNearby), resume = Light — the card turns into the import's progress (gallery.item.preview.importing.svg) and, when the last file lands with this project still in focus, PhotoViewerView takes the column with the Light panel open; 'Stay as Is' (role .cancel) changes nothing. WITH PICPLACE HOLDING THEM TOO (alsoOnPicPlace; desc-only): a third button, 'Download from PicPlace' (download(…, fromPicPlace: true) — the nearby device skipped), sits between the two, and the message ends ' The originals are on PicPlace too.' — five lines at 216 (the last 'are on PicPlace too.'), so the card is 260 × 270 at (545, 285); an NSAlert laid out with those words stacks the three the same way, 28 pt, 6 apart. The device's name is the other device's DeviceName.current (N5): a Mac's own computer name, a phone's model. THE ALERT IS APPKIT'S (macOS 26) and differs from the iPhone's (iOS/project-photo.viewer.preview.prompt.portrait.svg): measured on three Mac bench captures of 2026-09-25 (a photo's 'Download the full-size photo?', a collection's 'Download this clip?', a project screen's 'The originals aren't here' — the same metrics in each): a 260 pt glass card CENTRED ON THE WINDOW (not dropped from the title bar), radius ≈ 26, no app icon; the text left-aligned 22 pt in and wrapping at 216 pt (the three captures bound it to 213.3–223.2; 22 pt either side of the card is 216); the title 13 pt BOLD, its first baseline 32.5 under the card's top, a second line 16 below; the message 13 pt regular on 16 pt lines, in the label colour (not secondary); the two buttons full width, 16 pt in, 28 pt capsules 6 apart on black ~10 % — 'Import and Continue' over 'Stay as Is', both 13 pt REGULAR in the label colour: macOS 26 marks neither as default, so the first is marked by its place, not by the app's tint (the iPhone tints both labels); 16 pt under the last. The glass is drawn flat (#CDCDCF — what the measured glass gives over this dark poster; the captures' lighter pictures gave 216–225). With a two-line title and four message lines this card is 260 × 220 at (545, 310): the rule the template measured (20 · 16 per title line · 10 · 16 per message line · 16 · the buttons · 16), which an NSAlert laid out offscreen on this Mac reproduces field for field (title 16 per line, the message 16 per line, the stack 16 under it). THE VEIL: the whole window, title bar, filmstrip and tab bar included, goes to 102 + 0.4 × itself (measured: white → 204, #F0F0F5 → 198, black → 102) — a #AAAAAA layer at 60 %, not a black dim. The page under it is gallery.item.preview.nearby.svg's, unchanged — the nearby card (298 × 116) and tile 8's holdings-pill.nowhere.originals. OTHER OFFERS: gallery.item.preview.prompt.svg (.download and the rest); while the import runs the offer is .downloading with a source — 'Importing the originals' / '\(n) % so far from iPhone 18 Pro. Light can go ahead as soon as they are here.' · Continue When Ready · Stay as Is. A locked page's subject is 'The Text page' (…'Frames', 'Masks'). THE ITEM VIEW is gallery.item.svg's — the inspector column (GalleryPreviewPanel .inspector, 330 pt), the item header (▤ · ‹ Gallery · the name · 'n of N'), the editor column (the media beside the fixed 330 pt rail) and the filmstrip under everything, the floating tab bar — and GalleryItemEditor (App/GalleryItemView.swift) puts EditorPreviewPage in the editor's place when the focus request's asset is `.preview`: GalleryView.enterItem / move(to:) / step stage every project with `stageEditor(for:page:allowsPreview: true)`, so a preview opens, and the filmstrip and ← → walk straight through previews (they stalled on one until 2026-09-25). The page is its own view (EditorPreviewPageContent, plan T6), built from the editor's components with a `locked` state — never the editor mounted on a poster, so it has no write path (no persist net, no white migration, no as-shot reads). SAMPLE: tile 8 of gallery.svg's grid — 'Stack 7. 9. at 21:40', 8 of 14, 214 JPEG originals (3024 × 4032), 1,16 GB recorded in assets.ndjson — in gallery.item.preview.nearby.svg's state: pulled from PicPlace as a preview, its originals never uploaded, on the iPhone 18 Pro that shot them. LAYOUT (App/EditorPreviewPage.swift railBody, the Mac's only dressing): the picture pane — black, the whole 648 × 568 column (no timeline strip, no full-screen button, no marquee badge: the badge is the dark card's) — with poster.jpg as it is (previewPictureURL; graded when it was made, never graded again), scaledToFit and centred: 426 × 568 at x 462; a Divider; the rail, a ScrollView padded 14 / 16 / 20 with 12 between — RailTabBar (App/RailTabBar.swift, locked: Text · Frames · Masks accent at 38 %, Editor selected), EditorGroupBar (.macCard, locked: every cell #6D6D72 at 42 %, none selected, the dots LL.accent at 55 %), then statusCard(style: .light) at y 237 — LL.cardBackground, radius 16, padding 12, no badge. Every greyed control stays clickable and ASKS (a click on a locked page → ask(.tab), a group → ask(.group), the card itself → ask(.line), subject 'Editing' — only while it offers Download or nothing, never beside this offer's button). macOS rounds each Text frame up to the whole point (measured: the stage-1 captures' cards are 57 and 85 pt, exactly the rounded sums), so the rest card is 85 pt where the unrounded arithmetic says 83.7. HOOKS: the nearby bench (docs/nearby-originals-plan.md §12): a Mac scratch root (`-storage.libraryRootPath`) holding the preview — a pulled project, or `LL_DROP_SOURCES=<uuid>:originals` — and a Simulator holding the originals, both bound to one picplace.test account (`LL_PICPLACE_TOKENS` always, one token per install) and, before the server hands out the key, given the same `LL_NEARBY_KEY`; then `LL_TAB=gallery LL_ITEM=<uuid>` on the Mac with LetsLapse open on the Simulator; `LL_PREVIEW_PROMPT=light` raises this prompt 1.2 s after the page appears (its ':download' presses only a PicPlace offer), and a driver-launched Mac instance is pressed through accessibility, never the pointer — `~/Library/Developer/LetsLapseRun/tools/ax press <pid> '*' AXButton 'Import and Continue'`. The Mac copy needs Local Network permission (System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Local Network): refused, its browser and listener report NoAuth and the card never offers. Drawn from the code, not from a capture: a Mac importing is not benched yet (plan §15). The words are the code's; the alert's geometry is the template's measured rule, checked by laying these words out in an NSAlert offscreen; the wraps are CoreText's at 216.

g.data-symbol: camera.fill + a slash knocked through (no SF camera.slash)

g.text: The originals are only on iPhone 18 Pro

svg.text: macOS · Gallery · item view · a preview — the just-in-time prompt, the originals on a device nearby (Light clicked) · 1310×800 pt window
mirrors EditorPreviewPage ask(_:) + FetchPromptContent (.nearby) in AppKit's macOS 26 alert — LL_TAB=gallery LL_ITEM=<uuid> LL_PREVIEW_PROMPT=light on the nearby bench
